title: Average-Capacity Key Fraction Conjecture
summary: In the Gamma-modeled setting, illustrative ratios are below one half, but it remains open whether fewer than half of the keys have at least average capacity.

formal_statement.body: In the Gamma-modeled multidimensional linear-attack setting, let $K$ be the whole key space, let $C(k)$ denote the capacity associated with key $k$, and let $E_k[C(k)]$ denote the average capacity. The unresolved conjecture is whether fewer than half of the keys have capacity at least the average, namely whether $\left|\{k^* \in K : C(k^*) \ge E_k[C(k)]\}\right| < \frac{1}{2}|K|$; the task is to prove or refute this claim.

scope.domain: The problem concerns Gamma-modeled multidimensional linear cryptanalysis with key-dependent attack capacity.
parameters: C(k): the capacity associated with key k
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that the number of keys whose capacity is at least the average is less than half the size of the whole key space.

citations.label: Capacity and Data Complexity in Multidimensional Linear Attack

progress.summary: The paper presents the statement explicitly as Conjecture 1 and gives numerical ratios as illustrations. It provides no proof or refutation.
citation_labels: Jialin Huang et al., Capacity and Data Complexity in Multidimensional Linear Attack
